title: From AI pilots to scale: Improving the delivery of public services
gist: WDR 2026 authors lay out five steps for developing-country governments to move AI from pilots to scale: match AI to the problem, build AI-ready data, make pilots generate evidence, shift procurement from projects to products (with portability, interoperability, auditability), and invest in in-house capacity. Key evidence: only 17 of ~10,000 AI-health studies measured causal effects in low-resource settings, and 80% of surveyed LIC/LMIC governments lack meaningful AI evaluation.

insights.claim: Ghana's Rori math tutor delivered by text message produced nearly a full year of math learning gains at US$5 per student, and AI-supported imaging in Bangladesh raised daily diabetic retinopathy screenings by 39.5 percent.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Shows cheap AI interventions with measurable outcomes in EM public services.

insights.claim: For most governments the challenge is scaling AI from a few hundred users to millions, which requires better systems to buy, test, evaluate and integrate AI.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Govtech AI market growth depends on procurement and evaluation capacity, not model quality.
insights.locator: For most governments, the next step

insights.claim: Of nearly 10,000 studies of AI-based health interventions, only 57 were tested with real patients and providers in low-resource settings and only 17 measured causal effects.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Very thin evidence base; claims by health-AI vendors in EMs are largely unproven.
insights.quote: Of nearly 10,000 studies of AI-based health interventions, only 57 were tested with real patients and providers in low-resource settings.

insights.claim: In Thailand an AI diabetic retinopathy tool rejected more than 20 percent of images taken by nurses because clinic lighting and image quality did not match its training conditions.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Real-world deployment performance can diverge sharply from lab benchmarks; diligence risk for health-AI.

insights.claim: 80 percent of governments surveyed in low- and lower-middle-income economies report no or only basic mechanisms to evaluate AI performance.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Weak buyer evaluation raises both hype risk and future churn for AI vendors selling to EM governments.
insights.quote: 80 percent of governments surveyed across low- and lower-middle-income economies report having no or only basic mechanisms in place to evaluate AI performance

insights.claim: Putting AI on top of a poorly designed process can simply automate existing inefficiencies, so governments should first ask whether AI beats simpler alternatives and what complementary changes are needed.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Process redesign, not AI licenses, determines ROI.
insights.quote: Putting AI on top of a poorly designed process can simply automate existing inefficiencies.
insights.locator: Step 1: Match AI to the problem

insights.claim: Predictive AI suits agencies with large structured datasets and clear outcomes, as with revenue authorities using machine learning on tax returns to uncover compliance risks manual audits missed; generative AI suits language tasks like drafting, translation and citizen queries.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Tax administration is a proven entry point for predictive AI in government, implying revenue upside.

insights.claim: Brazil's VICTOR system, which converts scanned court documents into machine-readable text, cut the time to determine eligibility for appeal to the Supreme Federal Court from 40 minutes to 5 seconds.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Example of large productivity gains when government data is digitized.
insights.quote: has reduced the amount of time it takes to determine eligibility for an appeal to the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court from 40 minutes to just 5 seconds

insights.claim: Governments across developing economies cite data quality and availability as the most common barrier to using AI internally, requiring digitization of censuses, tax, civil, land and social-program records and cross-agency data links.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Data digitization and integration precede AI spend; opportunity for data-infrastructure vendors.

insights.claim: Traditional procurement treats technology as a one-off project, but AI systems need ongoing monitoring, maintenance, testing and improvement, so governments should shift to a product model with clear ownership and funding.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Favors recurring-revenue, service-based govtech contracts over one-off system builds.
insights.quote: Traditional government procurement treats technology like a one-off project
insights.locator: Step 4: Move from projects to products

insights.claim: Citing Jennifer Pahlka, the authors note most technology solutions could deliver 85 percent of required functionality at 10 percent of typical project cost if governments started smaller and iterated.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Iterative procurement could sharply cut public IT budgets, pressuring large system integrators.
insights.quote: most technology solutions could deliver 85 percent of required functionality at 10 percent of typical project cost
insights.locator: Step 4: Move from projects to products

insights.claim: Government AI contracts should require data portability, interoperability with existing systems and auditability of decisions.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Contract terms that reduce vendor lock-in and switching costs in public AI deals.
insights.quote: Data portability — so agencies are not locked into a single vendor
insights.locator: Step 4: Move from projects to products

insights.claim: Governments need in-house teams with authority and technical capacity, stable funding, external partnerships and broad civil-service AI literacy, with the most needed skills being understanding workflows, evaluating vendor claims and safely connecting government data.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Skills to evaluate vendor claims will make public buyers more demanding over time.

insights.claim: The authors frame scaling as a chain: pilots to evidence, evidence to institutions, institutions to lasting public value.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Expect multilateral AI lending to emphasize evaluation and institutional capacity over tool purchases.
insights.quote: Moving from pilots to scale means moving from pilots to evidence, from evidence to institutions, and from institutions to lasting public value.
